Title: SQL Injection in Product Search Functionality
Analysis:
The 'criteria' query parameter (`req.query.q`) is directly concatenated into a raw SQL query `SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name` without any sanitization or parameterization. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL statements.

Source: `req.query.q`
Sanitization/Validation: None except for a length truncation to 200 characters: `(criteria.length <= 200) ? criteria : criteria.substring(0, 200)`
Sink: `models.sequelize.query` via string interpolation.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /rest/products/search?q=test%27%20UNION%20SELECT%20*%20FROM%20Users%20--`
Snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name`)

Title: SQL Injection in User Login Functionality
Analysis:
The 'email' and 'password' request body properties are directly concatenated into a raw SQL query `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL` without parameterization or proper escaping, enabling SQL injection.

Source: `req.body.email`
Sanitization/Validation: None.
Sink: `models.sequelize.query` via string interpolation.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`POST /rest/user/login` with JSON payload:
`{ "email": "admin@juice-sh.op' --", "password": "" }`
Snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL`, { model: UserModel, plain: true })

Title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Profile Image URL Upload
Analysis:
The profile image upload from URL endpoint takes a user-supplied URL (`req.body.imageUrl`), validates nothing, and performs a GET request to that URL via `request.get(url)`. This exposes the server to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), allowing an attacker to coerce the server into requesting internal services (e.g., localhost endpoints or metadata servers) or internal IP ranges.

Source: `req.body.imageUrl`
Sanitization/Validation: None.
Sink: `request.get(url)`

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`POST /profile/image/url` with JSON:
`{ "imageUrl": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/" }` or `{ "imageUrl": "http://localhost:8080/admin" }`

Title: Open Redirect via Weak Allowlist Validation
Analysis:
The redirect target URL validation uses `url.includes(allowedUrl)` where `allowedUrl` is a permitted host from a predefined list. This allows an open redirect vulnerability because any URL that simply contains one of the allowed host URLs anywhere in it (e.g. as a query parameter or path segment, such as `https://attacker.com?redirect=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop`) will pass the validation check and the server will redirect the user to it.

Source: `req.query.to` (passed to `toUrl` in `routes/redirect.ts`)
Sanitization/Validation: `security.isRedirectAllowed(toUrl)` which performs `url.includes(allowedUrl)` in `lib/insecurity.ts`.
Sink: `res.redirect(toUrl)` in `routes/redirect.ts`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /redirect?to=https://attacker.com?https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop`

Title: Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Read via Poison Null Byte Bypass
Analysis:
In `routes/fileServer.ts`, public files are served via `res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file))` after checking if the filename ends with `.md` or `.pdf` (or matches `incident-support.kdbx`) and cutting off the poison null byte (`%00`). However, because it only checks if the input `file` contains forward slashes `!file.includes('/')` and does not check for backslashes on Windows platforms (or uses simple string manipulation instead of proper path resolution checks), directory traversal is possible on systems/servers accepting different path separators, or via the null byte termination bypass where `../../etc/passwd%00.md` can end with `.md` but when the null byte is cut off it becomes `../../etc/passwd`, allowing local file inclusion / path traversal.

Source: `req.params.file`
Sanitization/Validation: Checks `!file.includes('/')` and checks if it ends with `.md` or `.pdf`.
Sink: `res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file))` after `security.cutOffPoisonNullByte(file)` gets called.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /ftp/..%252f..%252fpackage.json%2500.md` (or double url encoded, or utilizing null byte directly depending on Node / OS) -> `package.json%00.md` -> cutOffPoisonNullByte makes it `package.json` after passing the `.md` validation. Or on Windows using backslashes like `..%5c..%5cpackage.json%00.md`.
